report.summary:
The package crucible/src/crucible/rapid now implements INTERFACE_CONTRACTS section 8. All work is committed on the branch and the tree is clean.

What works:
- **Actions and observations.** An `ActionSpace` covers all ten action kinds, each with a JSON schema and checks the schema cannot express. Observations are section-11 Observation dicts.
- **RapidEnv.** `make(family, seed, **difficulty)` builds a world. It handles action sequences, messages, a journal for filing predictions, joint plans, and controller programs run in `crucible.sandbox`.
- **Primitives.** A versioned registry of the 28 Part 7.1 primitives. Each is batched, never mutates its state, and has a characteristic-behaviour check (e.g. confounding shows passive slope > 1 but interventional slope about 0).
- **Generator.** `GraphBuilder` and `compose` cover 8 topologies, temporal classes, observation channels and affordances. The look-alike markets are four worlds with identical interfaces and different price rules; one intervention protocol tells them apart.
- **Engines.** Five, each with its own transition code: `primitive_graph` (vectorised compositional engine) plus four new Part 7.3 kinds: `discrete_event` (event heap), `graph_dynamical` (real networks), `state_machine` (hidden finite states) and `search`.
- **Fingerprints.** Measured from built worlds (9 components) with a distance. Renamed copies and parameter variants of all 29 families have distance 0. The smallest distance between real families is 0.063.
- **Admission.** Ten Part 7.4 checks, with oracles and references kept evaluator-side; world modules import none of them (checked in a fresh interpreter). Each check rejects a deliberately broken control world.
- **Families.** 29 families with intervention tests; 87 test runs, 0 failures.
- **4.0 view.** Lever families work as a 4.0 `Engine` (`engine="rapid"`), so `MechVecEnv` and the existing learners run on them unchanged.
- **Batch path and kernel twin.** `BatchRapid` steps many seeds at about 57,500 world-steps per second and matches single worlds bit for bit. Kernel-hosted `rig` twins with ledger money matched the fast simulators with 0 mismatches over 320 ticks.

Measured (seeds 0-2):
- 28 of 29 families admitted (21 train, 7 in the new v5-eval-1 partition), covering all 10 categories.
- 8 independent engines (5 v5 plus 4.0's scm, abm and techsys).
- 10 action modalities, 9 difficulty axes, 0 oracle-exposure findings.
- On held-out seeds 10-12: 26 of 29 admitted (19 train).

Below threshold, recorded as measured:
- M.1: 21 of 60 training families.
- M.2: 7 of 20 evaluation families.
- M.7 and M.8: 29 of 80 families.
- SP-7.3: 4 of 8 engine kinds.

Tests: 142 rapid unit tests and 15 gate tests pass. A run with the 4.0 rig, evaluator, research-env, learner, sandbox and admission tests plus the v5 checker and slots tests gave 314 passed. The full 1,076-test suite was not run.

limitations: Gate counts below threshold: M.1 has 21 of 60 training families; M.2 has 7 of 20 evaluation families; M.7 and M.8 have 29 of 80 families; SP-7.3 has 4 of 8 engine kinds.

Families were tuned against admission seeds 0-2. On held-out seeds 10-12, 26 of 29 are admitted: des_bottleneck and dl_short_term_damage fail the difficulty check there. net_cascade fails on both seed sets and is not admitted.

The difficulty check uses scripted public-information references, some generic (the best constant action found over practice episodes). A weak reference can fail a family that is not actually too hard.
Oracles are search-based upper references on the realised noise, not proven optima.
RapidEnv cash is unconstrained (it may go negative). Only the 4.0 lever view and the rig twin apply 4.0 money rules.
Structured-action families have no kernel module. The kernel twin exists only for lever families, through rig.
The informativeness check shows that observations depend on the hidden instance (between/within variance ratio, hidden-state predictability). It does not show that a learner can use them.
The structural generator `compose()` is tested over 8 topologies, but no registered family is built from a compose recipe yet. The families use `GraphBuilder` and `lookalike_market`.
Only the test subset listed was run, not the full 1,076-test regression suite.
integration_notes: Importing crucible.rapid.mechview registers a 4.0 mechanism engine 'rapid' in crucible.mechanisms.base.ENGINES. It adds no MECH_FAMILIES entries, so 4.0 splits, tasks and sealed sets are unchanged.
No kernel module was added (there is no rapid/modules.py), so load_all_modules is unaffected.

Contract functions are crucible.rapid.make, crucible.rapid.fingerprint(family) and crucible.rapid.admit(family, seeds). The fingerprint module is crucible.rapid.fingerprints (plural) so the function name is not shadowed. Registries are crucible.rapid.primitives.REGISTRY and crucible.rapid.families.REGISTRY.

Gate tests run admission on seeds 0-2 and 10-12 (about 60 CPU-s each, marked slow). Run them through crucible.scale.slots. Results are cached under $CRUCIBLE_CACHE/rapid/ keyed by a digest of the rapid sources (about 1 MB).
Env follows the section-11 Observation shape and offers observe/step/observe_since/tools/outcome, so workstream L can wrap it directly.
tests/test_v5_acceptance_checker.py rewrites the tracked docs/v5/evidence/checker_report.json when run. I restored it rather than committing it.
Generated evidence files were deleted locally; none were committed.
measurements: Admission of all 29 families on 3 seeds: about 60 CPU-s (1-4.5 s per family).
Seeds 0-2: 28 of 29 admitted (21 train, 7 eval). Seeds 10-12: 26 of 29 admitted (19 train, 7 eval).
Fingerprint minimum distance 0.063 (mk_elastic~mk_signal); 0 of 58 cosmetic variants counted.
Oracle exposure findings 0, with 852 hidden numbers scanned.
Batch path: 64 routing worlds x 30 ticks at about 57,500 world-steps/s; batch-vs-single mismatches 0.
Kernel twin vs fast simulator: 320 ticks compared over 4 families on 3 engines, 0 mismatches.
RapidEnv single world: about 0.3-1 ms per tick.
